req.title: Return 404 on unknown post
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-022 requires HTTP 404 when GET/POST /<id>/update or POST /<id>/delete references a non-existent post id. The pre-loaded fixture has exactly one post (id=1). Tests must: (1) positive — confirm existing post id=1 returns 200 on GET update (logged in as author); (2) negative — confirm non-existent id returns 404 on GET update; (3) boundary — id=0 (below minimum valid id) returns 404; additional tests cover POST update 404, POST delete 404, and id=2 (one above the only existing post) to catch off-by-one mutations. All tests log in as user 'test' (id=1, author of post 1) to satisfy login_required. Exact status code assertions (== 404, == 200) catch comparison-operator mutations. Both GET and POST methods are exercised to cover the full endpoint surface stated in the requirement.

tests.name: test_get_update_existing_post_returns_200
preconditions: App initialised with test database containing post id=1 authored by user id=1
trace: R-FLASKR-022: existing post id must NOT return 404
Catches mutations that flip the abort(404) condition to always fire
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_get_update_existing_post_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/1/update')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r.data

test_get_update_existing_post_returns_200()
